look: Battered: cracked faded leather with a stitched patch, dented tarnished latten chape, loose knotted lacing
prompt: Museum catalogue photo of a single object: an empty old battered medieval sword scabbard, 14th century, Baltic (Reval 1343), 82 cm long, once a decent burgher's scabbard, now worn out and mended. Straight, flat oval section 6 cm wide at the mouth narrowing to 3.5 cm at the tip. Wooden core covered in faded, cracked and scuffed brown leather, a patch of different darker leather stitched over a tear near the middle, edges rubbed pale; a dented tarnished latten chape at the tip, dull brown-green. Two narrow brown leather sword-belt tails, about 8 cm and 20 cm below the mouth, are laced around the scabbard in a loose criss-cross wrap, one knotted with a cord, cut off short, lying flat on its surface, nothing hanging. No studs, no buckles, no frog, no baldric, no ornament, not fantasy, no sword in it. Lying horizontally, mouth on the left and tip on the right, seen almost straight from above with a slight three-quarter tilt, whole object in frame with margin, plain pure white background, soft even studio light, no cast shadow, no hands, no people, no text.
